findings.F1: In a falling, calm market, where the close sits in its 20-day range predicts the next 3 days in the direction of the position, not back toward the middle. The excess 3-day return rises from −2.61 % and −2.50 % in the two lowest quarters of range position to +1.05 % and +1.54 % in the two highest. The slope's t is 2.67, with the cases of one day taken together (458 cases, 141 days). At 5 days the t is 2.07 (265 cases). The slope is positive in each year with enough cases: t 1.87 in 2018, 0.21 in 2019, 1.62 in 2021.
findings.F2: Over the next 5 days the calm-market nearness effect is stronger than over 3. On all calm bars the range-position slope has t 3.99 at 5 days (904 cases, 200 days) against t 2.91 at 3 days (1519 cases, 331 days). In choppy calm markets alone it is t 2.76 at 5 days (126 cases, 58 days) against t 0.87 at 3 days.
findings.F3: The book's trades earn far more when held longer. After fees, trades held 2 days or less average −1.19 % (median −2.36 %, 521 trades). Trades held 2 to 5 days average +0.35 %, 5 to 13 days +4.94 %, and over 13 days +12.77 % (479 trades). The edge needs time that a 3-day bet does not give it, which matters because the 3-day unusual move (+0.08 %) is below the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F4: The brief's reversion is not in choppy calm markets. On the 3-day grid, closes in the top fifth of the 20-day range average +0.37 % excess (44 cases), the middle −0.21 % (142 cases) and the bottom −0.99 % (28 cases). Closes near the top do no worse than the middle, and closes near the bottom do not rise.
findings.F5: In agitated markets, range position predicts nothing: the quintiles' excess 3-day returns range from −0.48 % to +0.40 %, with every t under 1. The day's own move reverses mildly only in falling, agitated markets (slope on the day's move in units of its 20-day swing, t −2.21, 274 cases, 75 days). That is the falling-agitated rebound the map already holds 12 times, so it is not a discovery.
findings.F6: Across weekdays, the next-day excess return after a Wednesday close is −0.45 % (t −2.60) and after a Friday close +0.37 % (t 2.85). Those t's count each coin separately on the same day. With seven weekdays looked at, and the map already holding a late-week gain (045-01), this does not stand out enough to count.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, calm market, the nearer a coin's close is to its 20-day high, the larger its rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: When a coin has neither trended nor swung much, a trader should read a close near the top of its 20-day range as a reason to be long for about a week, not as a reason to sell toward the middle.
ideas.name: choppy calm high continuation

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the nearer a coin's close is to its 20-day low, the larger its fall over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: In a quiet downtrend, a trader should treat a close near the bottom of the 20-day range as a reason to be short, or to refuse a long, for the next few days, rather than expecting a bounce.
ideas.name: falling calm low continuation
